overall_summary: The channel's clear performance leaders are extreme space anomalies and bizarre exoplanet conditions, particularly those highlighting extreme physics or weather (e.g., burning ice, coal-dark planets, and ruby rain). Conversely, generic psychology facts and repetitive brain-related topics consistently underperform, indicating audience fatigue with standard self-help or basic cognitive trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: TrES-2b ('The Planet Darker Than Coal') achieved 1,018 views and 36 likes. 'The Planet of Burning Ice' reached 1,055 views. 'Supersonic Rubies' hit 721 views and 25 likes. All leverage high-contrast, sensory-rich cosmic imagery.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space conditions, focusing on highly visual, hostile, or paradoxical environments (e.g., metal rain, evaporating planets) using a 19-21 second duration to maximize watch time.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' struggled across multiple uploads, peaking at only 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic cognitive facts. If psychology is explored, frame it through a high-stakes mystery or historical storytelling lens rather than clinical trivia.
